dedupe_keys.name: us national space weather strategy and action plan 2019 and implementation plan 2023

description: The National Space Weather Strategy and Action Plan sets US federal objectives and actions for a space-weather-ready nation. The March 2019 edition, which replaced the 2015 strategy and action plan, was produced by the interagency Space Weather Operations, Research and Mitigation (SWORM) working group under the National Science and Technology Council and published by OSTP. It has three objectives: enhance the protection of national security, homeland security and commercial assets, including assessing the vulnerabilities of critical infrastructures; develop and disseminate accurate and timely space weather characterisation and forecasts; and establish plans and procedures for responding to and recovering from space weather events, noting that events can cause direct or cascading failures across the 16 critical infrastructure sectors. The December 2023 Implementation Plan lists the agency actions to deliver the 2019 plan over five years, alongside the PROSWIFT Act and the Space Weather Advisory Group. Both are free downloadable PDFs in the public domain. Caveats: they are policy documents without data, the 2019 plan was due for review every four years, and later policy may supersede them. They support scoping of space weather impact scenarios and benchmarks for grid, satellite and GNSS resilience studies; related records are the NOAA SWPC products and the NERC geomagnetic disturbance standard.
